spec.title: Suraj Grid
spec.subtitle: From 0 to 100 Villages in 3 Years — Powering Rural India One Rooftop at a Time
spec.notes: Suraj Grid brings reliable, affordable solar electricity to rural villages that have lived in darkness for generations. We lead with our most impressive projection: 100 villages deployed within three years through word-of-mouth-driven growth. This is not just about power — it's about transforming lives, enabling education, economic opportunity, and safety after sunset. Today I'll show you how we're building the infrastructure that will light up 300 million lives across India.

slides.brief: Hero slide. Kicker: 'Solar Micro-Grid'. Title: 'Suraj Grid'. Subtitle: 'Powering Rural India — One Village at a Time'. Cinematic wide photo of a golden-hour Indian village with solar panels on rooftops and warm light spilling from windows. Speaker notes set the scene.

spec.title: 300 Million Lives on Pause After Dark
spec.notes: 300 million Indians lack reliable electricity — more than the entire population of the United States. In villages without grid power, life is constrained by daylight. Children cannot study after dark. Women cannot work evening shifts. Medical emergencies at night become life-threatening. Diesel generators are expensive, polluting, and unreliable. This quote captures the lived reality: electricity is not a luxury — it's the foundation for education, safety, economic mobility, and dignity. Suraj Grid exists to break this cycle.
spec.quote: When the sun sets, everything stops.

slides.brief: Open with the single most striking fact: 300 million Indians still lack reliable electricity. Quote a real villager-voice sentiment — 'When the sun sets, everything stops.' Attribution: Rural household survey, Rajasthan 2023. This earns emotional buy-in before the solution.

spec.title: Market Gap: The Scale of the Opportunity
spec.notes: The scale of India's rural energy gap is staggering: 650,000 villages still lack reliable grid access according to IAEA and MNRE data. This represents a $22B addressable market opportunity for distributed solar solutions. Even villages with nominal grid connection suffer 6-8 hours of daily outages — forcing families into expensive, polluting diesel generators or complete darkness. The human dimension: 300 million people live in this energy limbo every single day.

spec.title: Adoption Curve: 3-Year Village Rollout
spec.takeaway: From 2 villages in Q1 to 100 by end of Year 3 — compounding word-of-mouth growth (illustrative projection).
spec.notes: This chart shows our projected village deployment ramp-up over three years. We start conservatively with two pilot villages in the first quarter, focusing on perfecting installation and customer support. Success in these pilots triggers a referral effect — satisfied village champions become our best salespeople. By Q4 of year one, we're deploying to 18 villages. Growth accelerates in year two as our operational team scales and supply chain efficiencies kick in, hitting 48 villages by Q6. The third year is where compounding really shows: we cross 100 total villages by Q8, powered entirely by word-of-mouth and proven local credibility. This trajectory is ambitious but grounded in similar solar mini-grid rollouts across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

slides.brief: Column chart showing projected village deployments by quarter over 3 years: Q1 2, Q2 5, Q3 10, Q4 18, Q5 30, Q6 48, Q7 72, Q8 100. Label as illustrative projection. Takeaway: 'From 2 villages in Q1 to 100 by end of Year 3 — compounding word-of-mouth growth.'

spec.title: Business Model: Three Revenue Streams
spec.notes: Our business model is built on three sustainable revenue streams that align with village economics and government priorities. First, Pay-As-You-Go eliminates the upfront barrier that has stalled rural electrification for decades — villagers pay just ₹10-20 per day via UPI or SMS for the electricity they actually use, with no capital expenditure required. Second, government subsidies from MNRE and state DISCOMs covering up to 40% of installation costs significantly de-risks the capital outlay and makes our pricing competitive with diesel. Third, carbon credits from verified emission reductions provide additional revenue without affecting villagers — each 100-village cluster generates roughly 1,200 tonnes of CO₂ avoidance annually, worth ~$9,600 at current voluntary market prices. Together, these three streams create a resilient, scalable business that grows as impact grows.

cards.heading: Pay-As-You-Go
cards.text: ₹10-20/day via UPI/SMS, no upfront cost — villagers only pay for what they use, building a recurring revenue stream tied directly to consumption and adoption.

cards.heading: Government Subsidies
cards.text: MNRE & state DISCOMs co-fund installation up to 40%, reducing capital expenditure and making our system pricing competitive with diesel generators while aligning with national electrification goals.

cards.heading: Carbon Credits
cards.text: Verified emission reductions sold on voluntary markets at ~$8/tonne — each 100-village cluster generates ~1,200 tonnes CO₂ avoidance annually, adding ~$9,600 in non-tariff revenue per cluster.

slides.brief: Three cards: 1) Pay-As-You-Go (icon: zap) — villagers pay via UPI/SMS in micro-units, no upfront cost; 2) Government Subsidies (icon: landmark) — MNRE & state DISCOMs co-fund installation up to 40%; 3) Carbon Credits (icon: leaf) — verified offsets sold on voluntary carbon markets, ~$8/tonne. Each card has a concrete revenue mechanic.

spec.title: Impact: Light Changes Everything
spec.notes: These four before-vs-after contrasts capture the human transformation that electricity delivers. Study time: children currently lose the entire evening to darkness; LED lighting from Suraj Grid adds an estimated 4.2 usable hours. Women's enterprise: reliable power enables tailoring, food processing, and phone-charging businesses that were impossible after sunset — we project a 68% increase in women-led micro-business formation within 12 months of installation. Cost: households currently spend ₹60-80/litre on diesel; our pay-as-you-go solar tariff cuts that bill by roughly 35%. Environment: each village displacing kerosene and diesel avoids an estimated 1.2 tonnes of CO₂ annually. All figures are illustrative estimates based on comparable deployments in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia; actual impact measurement is built into our Cloud Dashboard from day one.

The third year is where compounding really shows: we cross 100 total villages by Q8, powered entirely by word-of-mouth and proven local credibility. This trajectory is ambitious but grounded in similar solar mini-grid rollouts across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

spec.title: Business Model: Three Revenue Streams
spec.notes: Our business model is built on three sustainable revenue streams that align with village economics and government priorities. First, Pay-As-You-Go eliminates the upfront barrier that has stalled rural electrification for decades — villagers pay just ₹10-20 per day via UPI or SMS for the electricity they actually use, with no capital expenditure required. Second, government subsidies from MNRE and state DISCOMs covering up to 40% of installation costs significantly de-risks the capital outlay and makes our pricing competitive with diesel. Third, carbon credits from verified emission reductions provide additional revenue without affecting villagers — each 100-village cluster generates roughly 1,200 tonnes of CO₂ avoidance annually, worth ~$9,600 at current voluntary market prices. Together, these three streams create a resilient, scalable business that grows as impact grows.

spec.title: Impact: Light Changes Everything
spec.notes: These four before-vs-after contrasts capture the human transformation that electricity delivers. Study time: children currently lose the entire evening to darkness; LED lighting from Suraj Grid adds an estimated 4.2 usable hours. Women's enterprise: reliable power enables tailoring, food processing, and phone-charging businesses that were impossible after sunset — we project a 68% increase in women-led micro-business formation within 12 months of installation. Cost: households currently spend ₹60-80/litre on diesel; our pay-as-you-go solar tariff cuts that bill by roughly 35%. Environment: each village displacing kerosene and diesel avoids an estimated 1.2 tonnes of CO₂ annually. All figures are illustrative estimates based on comparable deployments in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia; actual impact measurement is built into our Cloud Dashboard from day one.
